name: craft:robustness-at-boundaries
description: Is untrusted input validated where it enters, are failures surfaced rather than swallowed, and are secrets kept out of source? From the craft:robustness-at-boundaries skill.

artifact.type: code hunk (one function or diff hunk)

modules.name: input-validation
modules.purpose: Data from outside the program is parsed into a known shape before use.

readsExternalInput.instructions: Does this code read data from outside the program, such as a request body, file, environment variable, command-line argument or network response?

criteria.true: It reads at least one such source.
criteria.false: It only uses values passed in by other code or literals.

validatesBeforeUse.instructions: Before the external data is used, does the code check its shape or parse it into a typed value, rejecting it when it does not fit?

criteria.true: An explicit check, schema parse or type guard runs before use and rejects bad input.
criteria.false: The data is used directly, or only cast to a type without a runtime check.

castWithoutCheck.instructions: Does the code assert a type on external data without checking it at runtime, for example with a cast, a type-ignore comment or an any?

criteria.true: A cast or ignore stands in for a runtime check.
criteria.false: No such cast on external data.

notForJev.judgement: Is the same value validated again in other files?
notForJev.instead: Cross-file: grep the call graph in code, not a question about one hunk.

modules.name: error-handling
modules.purpose: Failures are handled or propagated with context, never silenced.

swallowsError.instructions: Does the code catch an error and then continue without handling it, re-raising it or reporting it?

criteria.true: An empty catch, a bare pass, an ignored error value, or a log line followed by the normal path.
criteria.false: Every caught error is handled, re-raised or returned.

failureSignalledByNull.instructions: Does the code signal a failure by returning null, -1 or an empty string instead of raising an error or returning an explicit result type?

criteria.true: A sentinel value stands for failure.
criteria.false: Failures raise or use an explicit result type, or there is no failure path.

errorMessageHasContext.instructions: How much does the error message raised here tell a reader about what failed?
criteria: No error is raised, or it has no message.
A generic message with no specifics.
Names what failed or includes the offending value.
Names what failed, the value, and what to do or the underlying cause.

modules.name: secrets
modules.purpose: Keys, tokens and environment-specific hosts come from configuration, not source.

literalSecret.instructions: Does the code contain a literal API key, token, password or private key written into the source?

criteria.true: A secret value appears as a literal.
criteria.false: Secrets, if any, are read from the environment or a secret store.

hardcodedHost.instructions: Which kind of network address does this code write as a literal?

criteria.production: A production or internal host written into the code.
criteria.local: Only localhost or a test fixture address.
criteria.none: No literal network address, or it cannot be told from this code.

compose.positive: no secrets or environment values in source

notForJev.judgement: Does a string match a known key format (sk-ant-, apikey_, lin_api_, AKIA...)?
notForJev.instead: A regex secret scanner in code: exact, free and not a judgement.
